P0_quantifier: computes over the ALGEBRA and its ARITHMETIC (rational/integral orbits of pairs of 27s under the Kato-Yukie group action). NOT over a manifold. Nothing here is a statement about m004, its class, its rows or its child.
the_gap: L138 FIRED (B969): the object's canonical pair -- the vacuum 3-block, the common kernel of the compact charges -- returns K exactly, 3/3. But Kato-Yukie classify ORBITS, and a VEV is a POINT. B969 stated the limit itself: 'within the orbit the choice remains free.'
why_the_orbit_cannot_be_narrowed_from_in: Let G act on the space V of pairs of 27s, and let O be a single G(Q)-orbit containing the object's pair v, with stabilizer S = Stab_G(v). Then EVERY point of O is G(Q)-equivalent to v BY THE DEFINITION OF AN ORBIT. So no invariant built from the G-action -- and the cubic etale algebra is exactly such an invariant, it is CONSTANT on the orbit, which is why it classifies orbits at all -- can distinguish one point of O from another. A canonical point inside O is therefore not merely unproved: it is UNREACHABLE by any orbit invariant. Asking the orbit invariant to pick a point is asking a class function to pick a representative.
what_this_rules_out: Sharpening the SAME invariant (a finer cubic, more primes, a better splitting statistic) cannot close the gap. Neither can a second orbit invariant. Every such move stays constant on O.

the_only_two_upgrade_routes.route_A_shrink_the_group: Replace G(Q) by a subgroup H that does NOT act transitively on O. Then O breaks into H-orbits and a canonical one may exist. The natural H is arithmetic: G(Z), or G(O_K) for the object's own field. This is EXACTLY B962's banked observation that 'over Z or a number field homogeneity FAILS' -- the same mechanism that made the arithmetic opening live in the first place. The number of G(Z)-orbits inside one G(Q)-orbit is a CLASS NUMBER-type quantity; if it is 1, the integral orbit IS a canonical point up to G(Z).
the_only_two_upgrade_routes.route_B_add_structure_the_orbit_does_not: Impose a condition that is NOT G-invariant -- a positivity/reality condition, an integrality lattice, or a compatibility with a second structure the object independently supplies. This breaks O by construction rather than by invariant.

the_concrete_next_computation: Route A is computable and is the programme's own kind of arithmetic: take the object's pair, which is already integral in the B854 Chevalley frame (unit structure constants, B884: 'every coefficient +-1'), and ask how many G(Z)-orbits sit inside its G(Q)-orbit. A class number of 1 would upgrade 'canonical orbit' to 'canonical point up to the integral group' -- which is exactly what a VEV direction needs, since a VEV is only ever defined up to the unbroken group anyway.
the_honest_prior: UNFAVOURABLE, and stated before computing. Class numbers of this kind are generically > 1, and the programme's own history (B962: OP^2 = F4/Spin(9) homogeneous; a canonical point of a homogeneous space exists only if the space is a point) is a record of homogeneity winning. What makes it worth running anyway is that the Q -> Z step is PRECISELY where B962 says homogeneity fails, so it is the one place the prior could be wrong for a stated reason.
VERDICT: X10 SHARPENED, NOT CLOSED. The orbit-to-point gap is NOT a gap in evidence -- it is STRUCTURAL: an orbit invariant is constant on the orbit, so it cannot pick a point, and no refinement of the SAME invariant ever will. Exactly two routes exist: SHRINK THE GROUP (Q -> Z, the arithmetic route B962 already identified as where homogeneity fails) or ADD NON-INVARIANT STRUCTURE. The concrete next computation is the count of G(Z)-orbits inside the object's G(Q)-orbit, with an honest UNFAVOURABLE prior.
